Class GuiController

java.lang.Object
com.tetris.ui.GuiController
All Implemented Interfaces:
GameView, javafx.fxml.Initializable
public class GuiController extends Object implements GameView, javafx.fxml.Initializable
The primary JavaFX Controller for the Tetris application.

This class implements the GameView interface and serves as the visual front-end of the application. It maps FXML elements to Java code, handles menu navigation, manages the scene graph layers, and delegates raw input events to the GameInputHandler.

    • setEventListener

      public void setEventListener(InputEventListener eventListener)
      Connects this View to the Logic Controller.

      Also initializes the GameInputHandler, providing it with the necessary callbacks to execute game actions (move, pause, new game) when keys are pressed.

      Specified by:
      setEventListener in interface GameView
      Parameters:
      eventListener - The controller interface to receive game events.

    • initGameView

      public void initGameView(int[][] boardMatrix, ViewData brick)
      Initializes the visual state of the game board.

      This calls the BoardInitiator to stack the necessary panes (Background, Ghost, Active Brick) and fills them with Rectangle nodes.

      Specified by:
      initGameView in interface GameView
      Parameters:
      boardMatrix - The initial state of the static background board.
      brick - The initial state of the active brick.

    • updateView

      public void updateView(DownData downData)
      Updates the UI after a "Down" event (Gravity or Soft Drop).

      This method checks if any rows were cleared in the process. If so, it triggers visual effects (Score notifications, Screen Shake, Particles). Finally, it refreshes the brick position.

      Specified by:
      updateView in interface GameView
      Parameters:
      downData - The result of the downward movement (contains clear info and brick position).

    • refreshBrick

      private void refreshBrick(ViewData brick)
      Refreshes the position and rotation of the active moving brick.

      This is the most frequently called update method (called every frame).

      Parameters:
      brick - The current state of the active piece.

    • handleInput

      private void handleInput(javafx.scene.input.KeyEvent event)
      Central routing method for keyboard input.

      Filters events:

      • Global Keys: 'M' for mute works anywhere (menus or game).
      • Game Keys: Movement keys only work if the game board is visible.
      Parameters:
      event - The JavaFX KeyEvent.
